scenes.tts: Suppose the heritability of height in a population is zero point six. Does that mean sixty percent of your own height comes from your genes? It does not. Heritability describes a whole population, not one person. To see why, start with variance.

scenes.narration: Suppose the heritability of height in a population is 0.6. Does that mean 60 percent of your own height comes from your genes? It does not. Heritability describes a whole population, not one person. To see why, start with variance.

scenes.tts: Variance is the average squared distance of values from the mean. Here is a population of adults, and heights vary from person to person. Take each person's distance from the mean, and square it. The average of those squares is the variance. One person alone has no spread, so one person has no variance.
scenes.visual: crowd with mean line, distance segments, squares; all but one person fade and the squares collapse
scenes.narration: Variance is the average squared distance of values from the mean. Here is a population of adults, and heights vary from person to person. Take each person's distance from the mean, and square it. The average of those squares is the variance. One person alone has no spread, so one person has no variance.

scenes.tts: Take a hypothetical height population, where the variance splits into genetic parts and an environmental part. Additive variance, the part that makes children resemble parents, is forty, from the average effects of alleles. Dominance variance is ten, interaction variance is zero, and environmental variance is fifty, so the total is one hundred. Narrow-sense heritability is additive variance over the total, forty over one hundred, which is zero point four. Broad-sense heritability adds the dominance part and gives zero point five.

Broad-sense heritability adds the dominance part and gives 0.5.

scenes.tts: Now improve nutrition in this population, and environmental variance falls from fifty to twenty. The genetic variance stays the same, so the total is seventy. Heritability is now forty over seventy, about zero point five seven. It went up, though no DNA changed. The units cancel, so heritability has none.

scenes.tts: High heritability does not mean fixed. Height is highly heritable within populations, yet average height rose across the twentieth century. In Richard Lewontin's analogy, a varied stock of seed is planted half in rich soil and half in poor. Within each tray, height differences are entirely genetic. The difference between the trays is entirely environmental.
scenes.visual: rising average-height line; then two seed trays, differences within each tray genetic, gap between trays environmental
scenes.narration: High heritability does not mean fixed. Height is highly heritable within populations, yet average height rose across the twentieth century. In Richard Lewontin's analogy, a varied stock of seed is planted half in rich soil and half in poor. Within each tray, height differences are entirely genetic. The difference between the trays is entirely environmental.

scenes.tts: So heritability within a group says nothing about why groups differ. It cannot split one person's height into genetic and environmental parts, because one person has no variance. Heritability is a ratio of variances in one population. Keep this rule. Heritability describes a population in an environment, never a person.
